title: Novel detection method for chemiluminescence derived from the Kinase-Glo luminescent kinase assay platform: Advantages over traditional microplate luminometers
author: Bell, Storey
materials: The location of GSK3 within the DEAE Sephadex fractions was determined by Western blot. SDS resolving gels (10% (v/v) acrylamide, 400 mM Tris, pH 8.8, 0.1% (w/v) SDS, 0.2% (w/v) ammonium persulfate (APS), 0.04% (v/v) tetramethylethylenediamine (TEMED)) were prepared with a 5% stacking gel (5% acrylamide, 190 mM Tris, pH 6.8, 0.1% (w/v) SDS, 0.15% (w/v) APS, 0.1% (v/v) TEMED). DEAE fractions were loaded into these gels and separated electrophoretically in SDS-PAGE running buffer (25 mM Tris-base, 190 mM glycine, and 0.1% (w/v) SDS) at 180 V for 45 min. 3 μL of Spectra™ Multicolor Broad Range Protein Ladder was added to one lane of every gel to act as molecular weight markers. Following electrophoresis, proteins were electoblotted onto polyvinylidiene difluoride (PVDF) membranes (Millipore) by wet transfer using transfer buffer (25 mM Tris, pH 8.5, 192 mM glycine, and 20% (v/v) methanol). The electroblotting was run at room temperature for 1.5 h at 160 mA.

Following protein transfer, the PVDF membranes were incubated overnight at 4 °C with GSK3-α/β antibody (Santa Cruz Biotechnology) diluted 1:1000 in Tris-buffered saline with Tween-20 (TBST; 20 mM Tris-base, 140 mM NaCl, 0.05% Tween-20) with a small amount of sodium azide added. After the overnight incubation, membranes were washed with TBST three times for 5 min each, which was followed by incubation with the anti-mouse secondary antibody conjugated with horseradish peroxidase (Bioshop Canada) at a dilution of 1:4000 in TBST. Membranes were incubated at room temperature for 1 h. Membranes were then washed three times for 5 min each time, and signal was then detected using enzymatic chemiluminescence (ECL). To initiate the membrane exposure 600 μL of hydrogen peroxide was mixed with 600 μL of luminol reagent on the membranes surface for several seconds. The mixture was then poured off and the chemiluminescence was detected ChemiGenius Bioimaging System (Syngene, MD, USA). Fractions identified to have GSK3 within them were then taken, pooled and held on ice until an affinity column could be constructed.

steps.title: Homogenize muscle and apply DEAE column
steps.instruction: Homogenize frozen skeletal muscle (13‑lined ground squirrel) 1:5 (v/v) in homogenization buffer (25 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0, 2.5 mM EDTA, 2.5 mM EGTA, 15 mM β‑mercaptoethanol, 25 mM NaF, 10 % glycerol); centrifuge at 13 500 × g for 30 min at 5 °C; collect supernatant and load onto a DEAE Sephadex column (6 cm × 1 cm) pre‑equilibrated with the same buffer; wash column with 20 mL homogenization buffer; elute bound proteins with a 0–2 M KCl gradient.

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE and transfer to PVDF
steps.instruction: Prepare 10 % resolving gel (400 mM Tris pH 8.8, 0.1 % SDS, 0.2 % APS, 0.04 % TEMED) with a 5 % stacking gel (190 mM Tris pH 6.8, 0.1 % SDS, 0.15 % APS, 0.1 % TEMED); load DEAE fractions, add 3 µL Spectra™ Multicolor Broad Range Protein Ladder to one lane; run electrophoresis in SDS‑PAGE buffer (25 mM Tris‑base, 190 mM glycine, 0.1 % SDS) at 180 V for 45 min; transfer proteins to PVDF membrane (Millipore) using wet transfer buffer (25 mM Tris pH 8.5, 192 mM glycine, 20 % methanol) at room temperature for 1.5 h at 160 mA.

steps.title: Immunoblot detection of GSK3
steps.instruction: Incubate PVDF membranes overnight at 4 °C with GSK3‑α/β antibody (Santa Cruz) diluted 1:1000 in TBST (20 mM Tris‑base, 140 mM NaCl, 0.05 % Tween‑20) containing a small amount of sodium azide; wash three times with TBST, 5 min each; incubate with HRP‑conjugated anti‑mouse secondary antibody (Bioshop Canada) diluted 1:4000 in TBST at room temperature for 1 h; wash three times with TBST, 5 min each; develop with ECL by mixing 600 µL hydrogen peroxide with 600 µL luminol reagent on the membrane for several seconds, pour off, and capture chemiluminescence using the ChemiGenius Bioimaging System.

steps.title: Affinity purification on blue‑agarose
steps.instruction: Equilibrate a blue‑agarose column (3 cm × 1 cm) in homogenization buffer; apply the pooled DEAE fractions containing GSK3; wash with 30 mL homogenization buffer; elute proteins with a 0–2 M KCl gradient; identify GSK3‑containing fractions by repeating Western blot as above.

steps.title: Concentrate GSK3 fractions
steps.instruction: Pool the GSK3‑positive fractions and concentrate them using 10 kDa cut‑off Amicon centrifugal filters by spinning at 8000 RPM for 20 min at 5 °C.

steps.title: Set up GSK3 kinase assay
steps.instruction: Prepare assay mixtures containing 50 µM ATP, 5 mM MgCl₂, GSK3 peptide (YRRAAVPPSPSLSRHSSPHQ(pS)EDEEE; SignalChem) at 0–185 µM, and 25 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5; optionally add 1 mM LiCl as a negative control; dispense reactions into 96‑well or 384‑well Costar black microplates; incubate kinase reaction for 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Detect activity with Kinase‑Glo
steps.instruction: Add Kinase‑Glo reagent to each well; let the plates sit for 10 min for the luminescent signal to stabilize; measure luminescence with the ChemiGenius Bioimaging System (same system used for the ATP standard curve).
